messages:
maya: Heads-up — we just saw a customer-facing spike in gen requests to eu-west1 at ~18:03 UTC. Autoscaler didn't bring up enough GPU nodes; several pods are Pending and canary fallback kicked to tiny-quantized model which is much slower for this workload :grimacing:
raj: seeing the same in metrics — queue depth jumped, scale_up_events not firing. k8s events show node provision requests but GCP quota errors for n1-standard-gpu-accelerators?
eli: pinging Cloud quotas now. Also noticed a flurry of spot preemptions in the pool right before the spike :thinking_face:
devops-bot: [autoscaler] scale_attempt at 18:03:15 -> requested 12 new nodes, provision_start 18:03:18, provision_fail: quotaExceeded (GPUs)
maya: exact logs? can someone paste the k8s event lines and the cloud error text?
raj: pasted snippet: ```Warning FailedScheduling  pod/transformer-xyz 0/12 nodes are available: 12 Insufficient nvidia-tesla-t4.```
eli: GCP error: ```Quota 'GPUS' exceeded for requested region 'europe-west1'. Current: 64, Requested: 76.```
maya: ok that explains provisioning stall. But why did autoscaler try to request that many at once? Our scale policy has aggressive surge for low-latency usecases. Could be thrash from ephemeral traffic burst.
sre-oncall: I increased cluster.maxUnready to 30 and manually queued a smaller incremental scale (requested 4) to unblock critical pods. Manual scale applied at 18:06 UTC.
raj: after manual request, some nodes showed up, but new pods hit InitContainer timeouts due to heavy image pulls — registry throttling. We need imageprefetch or smaller base images: the canary fallback plan saved CPU but not overall latency.
eli: two action items: 1) request GPU quota bump for eu-west1 (I've opened ticket to cloud console), 2) add a rate limiter to autoscaler to spread requests across 30s windows and cap per-cycle node requests to avoid giant single-shot provisioning.
maya: also toggle imagePullPolicy to IfNotPresent for non-canary images and enable node-local image cache on pools.
raj: note re: signal: our current load-signal uses 30s average. The spike was a 45s high-amplitude pulse; autoscaler interpreted rolling metrics as sustained and did big request. Recommend adding hysteresis and ignore pulses <60s for GPU pools.
sre-oncall: reopening the canary routing config to route 30% of traffic to eu-central as a cross-region fallback until region capacity stabilizes. Will monitor latency and cost.
devops-bot: [deploy] traffic-shift to eu-central (30%) executed at 18:12:40 UTC by pipeline/circuit-breaker v2
maya: cost note — cross-region burst increases egress and replica counts; finance FYI: this spike will show a temporary 2x GPU cost for affected customers.
eli: long-term: add a protective circuit in front of the autoscaler that checks quota and current preemption rate. If quota low or preemption >X, limit per-cycle provision size. I'll draft a PR.
raj: for the postmortem: log these things: quota check before scaling, rate-limited scale requests, image preload, adjust signal window, and an oncall runbook step to fall back to alternate region.
sre-oncall: monitoring: I've pinned a dashboard for eu-west1 GPU quota and preemption count plus a pager if scale_attempts fail 3x in 10m.
maya: thanks all. Keep posting any residual errors. I'll start the incident note and flag in #incidents. :thumbsup:
